title: Exceptions, Result, and handling failure without throwing

videos.script: A student types forty where a number should be. A file the planner expects is not there. A timer is stopped before it was started. Three failures, and they are not the same kind. {{throw}} This lesson starts with exceptions, and the one thing Kotlin removed from Java's: checked exceptions. You will read a stack trace from the bottom up. {{try}} Try as an expression, finally that always runs, and why catching every exception turns a bug into a zero. {{use}} Use, which closes a file even when the code reading it fails. {{require}} Require and check, which throw with a sentence that says whose mistake it was. {{result}} Then Result: a failure you hold as a value, and the trap in run catching. {{choose}} And the question that decides between all of them. If this happens, whose code is wrong?
